name: Ashes
overview: Scripture presents ashes as a profound symbol of human frailty and the need for repentance, as Abraham humbly refers to himself as 'dust and ashes' (Genesis 18:27) and Genesis 3:19 reminds us of our return to dust. Ashes also serve a practical and spiritual role in purification, as seen in the detailed instructions for using the ashes of the red heifer to cleanse from sin (Numbers 19:9, 19:10, 19:17). Additionally, ashes are associated with mourning and repentance, exemplified by Mordecai wearing sackcloth and ashes while crying out in distress (Esther 4:1). These uses collectively reveal ashes as a tangible expression of humility, sorrow, and the cleansing work necessary before God.
